diagnosis: Right eye: Acute primary angle-closure glaucoma (severe); Left eye: Advanced open-angle glaucoma

history.name: EF
history.presenting_complaint: Severe headache and haloes around lights for one day, with very blurry vision in the right eye and associated nausea.

history_of_presenting_illness.symptom_progression: Severe headache, haloes, and blurred vision worsening throughout the day.
history_of_presenting_illness.associated_symptoms: Nausea, photophobia, mild vomiting; no trauma.
history_of_presenting_illness.chronic_context: Known glaucoma for several years with variable adherence to medications.

history.past_ocular_history: No ocular surgery. Mild cataract noted previously.
history.general_health: Cardiovascular risk factors present; otherwise well.
history.social_history: Retired individual; mild falls risk at home.

examination.pupils: Right pupil sluggish and mid-dilated (~4.5 mm); left 2 mm, reactive.
examination.anterior_segment_gonio: RE: closed angles; LE: open to 3–4 quadrants; OU: mild nuclear sclerosis.
examination.fundus: RE cup-to-disc ratio 0.9 with diffuse rim loss and disc haemorrhage; LE C/D 0.8 with rim thinning.
examination.perimetry: HVF mean deviation -18 dB both eyes (marked constriction), results align with fundus and OCT findings.

plan_summary: Urgent treatment of right eye acute angle-closure: topical timolol, brimonidine, dorzolamide; oral acetazolamide 500 mg stat then 250 mg QID; topical prednisolone acetate 1%; pilocarpine once IOP reduced; IV mannitol if refractory. Perform laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) RE within 24–48 h; consider prophylactic LPI LE. Long-term: fixed-combination drops, possible SLT for LE, and trabeculectomy or tube shunt RE if control inadequate. Advise avoidance of mydriatics and close follow-up with target low IOP.
case_notes: 65M; 1-day severe headache, haloes, nausea; RE very blurry; inconsistent latanoprost/timolol; cardiovascular risk factors; FHx brother with glaucoma. VA 6/38 RE (no pinhole improvement), LE 6/12→6/9; pupil RE sluggish 4.5 mm; gonio: RE closed, LE 3–4; IOP 55/20 (GAT); CCT 495/500 µm; discs: C/D 0.9 RE, 0.8 LE, rim loss, haemorrhage RE; HVF MD −18 dB OU; OCT RNFL thin. Dx: RE acute PAC on severe glaucoma; LE advanced OAG. Treat RE urgently, LPI RE, prophylactic LPI LE, consider surgery if control poor.

history_taking: Chief Complaint and associated systemic symptoms (headache, haloes, nausea)
Onset and time course of visual symptoms
Red-Flag Screen: severe eye pain, haloes, vomiting, decreased VA, photophobia
Past ocular and systemic history including medication adherence
examination: Slit-lamp: corneal clarity, anterior chamber depth, lens status
Dilated fundus exam: optic disc cupping, rim loss, haemorrhages
OCT and perimetry for RNFL and visual field status
diagnosis_and_management: Identify acute primary angle-closure glaucoma and differentiate from chronic open-angle glaucoma
Immediate management: pressure-lowering drops (timolol, brimonidine, dorzolamide), oral acetazolamide, pilocarpine after IOP drop, pred acetate, IV mannitol if refractory
Plan definitive management: LPI RE, prophylactic LPI LE, surgical options if control inadequate
Long-term management: fixed-combo drops, SLT, trabeculectomy/tube RE
Provide patient education and mydriatic avoidance advice
infection_control: Hand hygiene, PPE, and instrument cleaning during tonometry, gonioscopy, or LPI preparation
documentation_and_handover: Document IOP values, medications used, timing and doses
Record gonioscopy findings, cup-disc ratios, CCT, and HVF results
Handover plan for urgent LPI and systemic management

emotional_affect: Acutely distressed and anxious, photophobic, nauseated, and pain-guarding. Expresses fear of imminent vision loss and guilt about inconsistent medication adherence. Alert and oriented but distracted by pain. Responds well to calm, brief explanations and clear management steps. No suicidal ideation disclosed.
